name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd
title: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd - 543950 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 revenue INR 3,416m (+47% YoY) and occupancy 71%, but group is in heavy bed expansion (3,200 beds, target 5,000) with 70% of new beds via acquisition and ramp-up losses at new hospitals.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to INR 3,416 million and EBITDA hit a record INR 799 million at a 23.4% margin.
summary.overview: Yatharth reported record quarterly EBITDA and revenue growth of 47% YoY in Q4 FY26, with FY26 revenue up 36% to INR 12,072 million. New hospitals (New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra) ramped faster than expected, though they still drag EBITDA. Management reiterated 5,000 beds in three years, a 24-25% margin band, and FY27 growth above 36%. Management also disclosed a CGHS rate revision adding about 5% to revenue from December onwards.

segments.name: Noida Extension
segments.commentary: Q4 ARPOB INR 47.8k (+23% YoY, highest ever); occupancy 61% on 390 census beds, 450 capacity. Oncology share reportedly rose to about 30% from 19-20%.

segments.name: Greater Noida
segments.commentary: Q4 ARPOB INR 40.3k (+15% YoY); occupancy 76% on 330 census, 400 capacity. Brownfield expansion under way.

segments.name: New hospitals (New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra)
segments.commentary: New Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 together contributed about 11% of Q4 revenue; ARPOB about INR 40k each. Agra (250 beds, integrated Feb 2026) runs about INR 7 crore monthly revenue, ARPOB about INR 26-27k, and an EBITDA margin around 18%.

segments.name: Jhansi-Orchha
segments.commentary: Occupancy 86% on 250 census of 305 capacity; ARPOB below group average, per management not material to group.

segments.name: Greater Faridabad
segments.commentary: Occupancy 69% on 150 census of 200 capacity; Q4 ARPOB INR 31k; turned profitable in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to exceed FY26's 36%, and FY27 EBITDA growth also expected to exceed FY26.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance of 24-25% maintained; management expects FY27 margin to be better.
Target of 5,000 beds in three years (about 3,200 beds now announced); management says it could come earlier. About 70% of upcoming beds via acquisitions, 30% greenfield.
Debtor days target of 90-95 days for FY27.
Gurugram Sector 40 hospital (acquired, under construction): operational by April 2027, ARPOB above INR 50k, break-even about 15 months after operationalisation.
New Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 expected to reach combined EBITDA breakeven in H2 FY27; Faridabad about 10-11 months, Delhi 14-15 months.
Government payer mix to fall from about 35% toward 25% over about two years; new hospitals target no more than 10-12% government business.
Brownfield capex about INR 75 lakh per bed at Greater Noida and Noida Extension, excluding land; no cost escalation expected. No fund raise planned for the 5,000-bed plan.

qa_highlights.question: Operating metrics for new hospitals and Jhansi; reason for interest cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Model Town occupancy 32% (300 capacity), Faridabad new 52%, Agra 52%. Jhansi 85-86%, ARPOB below group average but immaterial. Interest rise attributed to loans taken for Agra.

qa_highlights.question: Break-even timing for New Delhi and Faridabad new hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Faridabad Sector 20 in about 10-11 months; Delhi in 14-15 months. Combined EBITDA breakeven expected in H2 FY27. Current EBITDA losses: Delhi INR 21 crore, Faridabad INR 9 crore, about 2% drag on net losses.

qa_highlights.question: CGHS benefit quantum, and why Q4 figures differ from earlier estimates?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-quarter benefit about 4.5-5% of revenue; the 1.7% figure reflected only partial implementation in the quarter the revision began. Full effect expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Gurugram break-even and speciality mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Tertiary and quaternary focus, more self-pay and insurance, less government business. Break-even about 15 months from operationalisation, expected to be operational around April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Brownfield cost per bed and energy-cost risk?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 75 lakh capex per bed excluding land; no cost escalation expected.

qa_highlights.question: Income tax matter status?
qa_highlights.answer: Near final; some assessment orders received with no major liability expected. Resolution expected by end of Q2 FY27; no FDs or assets frozen.

risks_watch: Government share (about 35%) and CGHS rate dependence; pricing caps on oncology drugs.
Ramp-up losses at New Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 until H2 FY27 breakeven; Gurugram adds further loss-making ramp-up.
International patient softness from West Asia disruption and border closures; recovery is management's assumption.
Debt rising for Agra and new capex, with interest cost up sequentially; debt and net cash figures were stated inconsistently on the call.
Pending income tax matter; management says resolution expected by end of Q2 FY27.
Debtor days target of 90-95 in FY27 from 112 in FY26.
Acquisition-led growth (about 70% of the 5,000-bed plan) carries integration and pricing risk.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin (ex ramp-up losses)
FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin (ex ramp-up losses)

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,160 million; total cash INR 3,931 million

capex_capacity: Total bed capacity above 3,200 beds with Gurugram and brownfield expansions; about 2,500 beds operated currently.
Gurugram Sector 40 acquisition: upfront about INR 100 crore plus about INR 100 crore for finishing and medical infrastructure.
Brownfield expansions at Greater Noida (structural drawings finalised, basic construction started) and Noida Extension (legal formalities completed, earlier phases).
Agra hospital: 250 beds, Da Vinci robot installed, 50 robotic surgeries completed.

Debt about INR 230 crore; net debt about INR 116 crore per one answer, while another answer cites net cash of INR 115 crore. Management plans some additional debt, funded largely by internal accruals.
demand_pricing: CGHS revised rates from December 2025: about 5% uplift to overall revenue, with more than 3% flowing to EBITDA; full effect expected in FY27.
Oncology is about 10% of group revenue; capped pricing on certain oncology drugs cut revenue by about 20-30% on that portion, per management. Management called the impact marginal.
West Asia disruption and closures in Bangladesh and Afghanistan reduced international patient flows in the prior 3-4 months; management expects recovery in Q1 FY27 and is pushing Africa.
Government payer mix about 35% (CGHS, ECHS, ESI at CGHS rates), with cash and TPA the rest; down 2-3 points YoY.
Interest cost rose sequentially on loans taken for Agra.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, ARPOB and the 5,000-bed target. Evasive or vague on specifics: debt figures were inconsistent, the Agra break-even was not quantified, and the oncology impact was softened.
key_quotes: We remain confident of achieving our target of 5,000 beds over the next three years.
So, we feel that in fact, from this financial year, EBITDA margins, next financial year EBITDA margins should actually be better.
It is a profitable hospital and it is having an EBITDA margin of already 18%.
